samples.summary: CLI login now hard-fails (30s hang, then a misleading "Login timed out") whenever the backend does not echo `state`
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer(expectedNonce)` returns 400 for any callback whose `state` does not equal the nonce (login.ts:206-210), and the promise stays pending, so the only outcome is the 30s timeout at login.ts:257 rejecting with 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.'. The echo is optional on the server side: auth.controller.ts:130-132 only appends `&state=` when `state.nonce` is set, and github-auth.guard.ts:33-38 stores `undefined` for any nonce that is absent, non-string (e.g. `?nonce=a&nonce=b` yields an array) or longer than 128 chars. So a new CLI talking to a backend that predates this change — or any deployment/proxy that drops the extra query param — cannot log in at all, and the terminal reports a timeout rather than the real cause (the browser sees only the bare body 'Invalid state'). No fallback, no diagnostic, and no version negotiation exists.

samples.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` discards the server's error message for bodies whose `error` is not an object (e.g. Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error: "Not Found"}`)
samples.evidence: `raw = data?.error`; when `raw` is a string (Nest's default exception body puts the reason phrase in `error` and the real text in `message`), the `typeof raw === 'object'` test at formatter.ts:101 fails, `fields` is `{}`, and the emitted envelope becomes `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. The call sites still gate on truthiness of `error` (docs.ts:197, docs.ts:267, notes.ts:150/215, slides.ts:156/216), so this path is taken exactly where the old code printed the body verbatim and preserved `body.message` (including ValidationPipe's message array). Backend endpoints that are not hand-shaped (`{error:{code,message}}`) therefore lose their diagnostic text on `docs content`, `docs export`, `notes/slides content`, `files upload/download` and the import orchestrators.

samples.summary: `files download` reports `HTTP_ERROR` / `"HTTP 200"` when the response is ok but carries no bytes
samples.evidence: The guard is `!res.ok || !res.bytes`; in the second case `res.status` is 200, so the fallback message renders `HTTP 200` next to code `HTTP_ERROR` — a self-contradicting envelope. Previously the emitted body was `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` with no message, so the change actively introduces the wrong status text on this branch.

samples.summary: `runCli` mutates the caller-supplied program by registering a `preAction` hook on every invocation, and `acting` is never reset
samples.evidence: `program.hook('preAction', ...)` is registered inside `runCli`, so calling `runCli(sameProgram, argv)` twice (tests do pass a program in) accumulates duplicate hooks on the shared object; each closure writes to its own `acting`, so a later invocation cannot clear an earlier one. Also, if a throw escapes after the action completed (or from a second parse), `acting` still holds the last command that ran, so the envelope can attribute an error to a command that was not the one failing.

samples.summary: New login-callback test may leave the HTTP server handle alive: `close()` calls `srv.close()` without destroying the keep-alive sockets undici's `fetch` holds
samples.evidence: The test issues three `fetch` calls against the loopback server; Node's global undici agent keeps those connections alive. `close()` in `startCallbackServer` (login.ts:280-283) only calls `srv.close()`, which refuses new connections but does not destroy existing sockets, so the server handle can stay referenced until the idle sockets time out — a hanging-handle/leak risk for the vitest worker (and, in the real CLI, a delayed process exit after login).

samples.summary: An out-of-range or repeated `nonce` query param is silently downgraded to `undefined` instead of rejected, turning a client mistake into an opaque CLI timeout
samples.evidence: `typeof nonce === 'string' && nonce.length > 0 && nonce.length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH ? nonce : undefined` — a 129-char nonce or `?nonce=a&nonce=b` (array) yields `undefined`, the controller then omits `&state=` (auth.controller.ts:130), and the CLI rejects its own genuine callback with 400 and waits out the 30s timeout. Failing the request with a 400 at the guard would surface the cause; fail-open here is indistinguishable from a legitimate no-nonce flow.

finding.summary: CLI login now hard-fails (30s hang, then a misleading "Login timed out") whenever the backend does not echo `state`
finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer(expectedNonce)` returns 400 for any callback whose `state` does not equal the nonce (login.ts:206-210), and the promise stays pending, so the only outcome is the 30s timeout at login.ts:257 rejecting with 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.'. The echo is optional on the server side: auth.controller.ts:130-132 only appends `&state=` when `state.nonce` is set, and github-auth.guard.ts:33-38 stores `undefined` for any nonce that is absent, non-string (e.g. `?nonce=a&nonce=b` yields an array) or longer than 128 chars. So a new CLI talking to a backend that predates this change — or any deployment/proxy that drops the extra query param — cannot log in at all, and the terminal reports a timeout rather than the real cause (the browser sees only the bare body 'Invalid state'). No fallback, no diagnostic, and no version negotiation exists.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. login.ts:206-210 returns 400 and returns early for any callback whose `state` does not equal the nonce, and `nonceMatches` (login.ts:164-169) treats a missing `state` as a mismatch (`if (!received) return false`). `callbackResolve` is only reached at login.ts:251-254, after that gate, so a callback lacking the echo leaves `callbackPromise` pending; the sole remaining settle path is the 30s timer at login.ts:257-265 rejecting with 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a cause-obscuring message for what is actually a missing echo. The echo is genuinely optional server-side: auth.controller.ts:130-132 appends `&state=` only when `state.nonce` is truthy, and github-auth.guard.ts:33-39 stores `undefined` whenever the nonce is absent, non-string (duplicated query param yields an array in Express) or longer than MAX_NONCE_LENGTH (128, github-auth.guard.ts:6). The CLI unconditionally mints and sends a nonce (login.ts:42, :46) and therefore unconditionally requires the echo, with no fallback, diagnostic, or version negotiation anywhere in packages/cli. Result: against a backend that predates this change, or in the guard's reject-to-undefined cases, login can never succeed and fails as a 30s hang plus a misleading timeout — a mis-handled failure path in the correctness lane, not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope. (The in-repo matched-version path does work, since a 43-char base64url nonce passes the guard, which bears on severity but not on the finding's validity.)

finding.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` discards the server's error message for bodies whose `error` is not an object (e.g. Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error: "Not Found"}`)
finding.evidence: `raw = data?.error`; when `raw` is a string (Nest's default exception body puts the reason phrase in `error` and the real text in `message`), the `typeof raw === 'object'` test at formatter.ts:101 fails, `fields` is `{}`, and the emitted envelope becomes `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. The call sites still gate on truthiness of `error` (docs.ts:197, docs.ts:267, notes.ts:150/215, slides.ts:156/216), so this path is taken exactly where the old code printed the body verbatim and preserved `body.message` (including ValidationPipe's message array). Backend endpoints that are not hand-shaped (`{error:{code,message}}`) therefore lose their diagnostic text on `docs content`, `docs export`, `notes/slides content`, `files upload/download` and the import orchestrators.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. formatter.ts:100-103 only copies fields when `data.error` is a non-array object; otherwise `fields` is `{}` and code/message fall back to the caller's values (105-110), discarding the body's top-level `message`/`statusCode`. The path is reachable: http-client.ts:184-185 (and 248-249, 261-267) hands the raw server JSON through unmodified, and the backend has no global exception filter (main.ts:65-72 installs only ValidationPipe; no APP_FILTER/ExceptionFilter anywhere in packages/backend/src), so HttpExceptions such as document.controller.ts:169 `NotFoundException('Document not found')` serialize as Nest's default `{statusCode,message,error:"Not Found"}`. Because `error` is the truthy string "Not Found", the call-site guards at docs.ts:197/267, notes.ts:156, slides.ts:162 enter the backend-envelope branch (files/download.ts:62-70 and files/upload.ts:229 call it unconditionally), so the emitted envelope is `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` and the server's diagnostic text — including ValidationPipe's message array on 400s — is lost. Existing tests only cover object-shaped `error` bodies and a null body, so nothing guards this case. In-lane for correctness (error handling that swallows failure detail); major impact.

finding.summary: backendErrorEnvelope silently discards non-`{error:{…}}` backend bodies, losing the server's message (Nest default error shape)
finding.evidence: `const raw = data?.error; const fields = raw && typeof raw === 'object' && !Array.isArray(raw) ? {...raw} : {}` (formatter.ts:99-103). NestJS's default HttpException body is `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document not found","error":"Not Found"}` — `error` is a STRING, so `fields` becomes `{}` and the emitted envelope is only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. No global exception filter shaping `{error:{code,message}}` exists in packages/backend/src (grep for `ExceptionFilter` returned nothing; only hand-written bodies like TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY in docs-content.controller.ts:42 use that shape). Before this change every call site printed `JSON.stringify(res.data ?? …)` verbatim, so the user saw `message`. Now the actual failure reason is dropped on the most common backend error shape, across files/upload.ts:229, files/download.ts:64, docs/import.ts:178/215/238, notes/import.ts:168/201/220, slides/import.ts:197/247/268. Also note docs.ts:267 / notes.ts:150 / slides.ts:156 gate on `if (body?.error)`, which is truthy for the string `"Bad Request"`, so that branch is taken and the detail is lost rather than falling through.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. formatter.ts:99-103 only copies fields when `data.error` is a non-array object; for NestJS's default HttpException body (`{statusCode, message, error:"Not Found"}`) `error` is a string, so `fields` is `{}` and both code and message fall back to `HTTP_ERROR`/`HTTP <status>`, discarding the server's `message`. I verified no global exception filter or @Catch handler exists anywhere in packages/backend/src (grep for ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|@Catch: no matches), and that real reachable endpoints throw plain string exceptions: document.service.ts:33 (`NotFoundException('Document not found')`), files.controller.ts:74/81/141/177, docs-content.controller.ts:138/151/228+, tabs.controller.ts:44/89/122. Only docs-content.controller.ts:88 uses the hand-written `{error:{code,message}}` shape (TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY at :42-47). The CLI client does not reshape bodies — http-client.ts:184-185/248-249/265/369-370 pass `await res.json()` through verbatim — so the default shape reaches backendErrorEnvelope unaltered at upload.ts:226-236, download.ts:64, docs/import.ts:179/215/238, notes/import.ts:168/201/220, slides/import.ts:198/247/266. The reviewer's secondary point also holds: docs.ts:197 and :267 (and notes.ts:156/217, slides.ts:162/219) gate on `if (body?.error)`, truthy for the string "Not Found"/"Bad Request", so the lossy branch is taken instead of falling through to `throw new Error`. This is swallowed/mis-handled error detail on a common real path — in the Correctness lane and blocking at major.

finding.summary: CLI unconditionally requires a `state` echo the backend may not send — login then hangs 30s and fails with an unrelated timeout message
finding.evidence: login.ts:206 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, but the backend only appends it conditionally: `const stateEcho = state.nonce ? \`&state=…\` : ''` (auth.controller.ts:130). `state.nonce` is undefined whenever GitHubAuthGuard dropped it — non-string (duplicate `?nonce=a&nonce=b` makes express give an array), empty, or >128 chars (github-auth.guard.ts:34-38) — and, more importantly, whenever the CLI runs against a deployed backend that predates this change. In all those cases the genuine callback is answered with HTTP 400 'Invalid state', the promise never settles, and the user waits the full 30s for 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a message that gives no hint of the real cause. There is no negotiation, version check, or diagnostic for the nonce-absent case.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the reviewer describes. login.ts:206 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and nonceMatches (login.ts:164-169) returns false for a *missing* state too, so a genuine callback that carries no `state` is 400'd and the promise is intentionally left unsettled (comment at login.ts:203-205). The only other exit is the 30s timer (login.ts:257-265) whose message ('Login timed out...') gives no hint of a state mismatch, and no log/diagnostic is emitted on the 400 path. On the backend the echo is genuinely conditional — auth.controller.ts:130-132 builds `stateEcho` only when `state.nonce` is truthy, yet still mints a code (line 126) and redirects (line 133-135); github-auth.guard.ts:34-38 stores `undefined` for a non-string/empty/>128-char nonce, and cli-auth.store.ts:13,60 propagates it as optional. No guard elsewhere makes the nonce-absent echo branch unreachable. The current CLI always sends a valid 43-char nonce (login.ts:42,46), so same-version pairs work; but packages/cli/package.json shows an independently published, versioned binary (@wafflebase/cli 0.6.4 with bin/files), making new-CLI/old-backend skew a real path where login cannot succeed and fails with an unrelated timeout message. Mis-reporting a failed login as a timeout with no diagnostic sits inside the correctness lane (error handling that mis-handles failures). My only doubt is severity, not reality, so the finding stands.
